name: Vermont veterans: Office of Veterans Affairs for claims help
description: Free help applying for VA benefits from the Office of Veterans Affairs’ Veteran Service Officers in Montpelier, who serve the whole state. Certified service officers from the American Legion, VFW and DAV also help any veteran apply; membership is not required.
next_step: Call 802-828-3379 or, within Vermont, 888-666-9844 (weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Or call a service officer: American Legion 802-296-5166, VFW 802-296-5168, DAV 802-296-5167.
constraints: Call before visiting; the office serves the whole state from Montpelier.

source_evidence.title: Vermont Office of Veterans Affairs: Contact Information for Organizations that Help Veterans and Their Families
source_evidence.scope: Office address, main and toll-free lines, hours, and the certified Veteran Service Officers of the American Legion, VFW and DAV; read in full.

name: Vermont Area Agencies on Aging and the Senior HelpLine
organization: Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging
description: Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging give information and help to people 60 and older and their families: help at home, meals, caregiver support, health insurance counseling and more. One statewide HelpLine reaches all five. Military service is not required.
next_step: Call the Senior HelpLine at 1-800-642-5119, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

source_evidence.scope: The five agencies’ service areas and the statewide line, 1-800-642-5119; read in full.

name: Medicare counseling (Vermont SHIP)
organization: Vermont State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Area Agencies on Aging
description: Free, confidential Medicare counseling from certified counselors at Vermont’s five Area Agencies on Aging: plan choices, Part D, Medigap and help paying for Medicare. The Senior HelpLine connects you to a counselor near you.
next_step: Call the Senior HelpLine at 1-800-642-5119 and ask for a SHIP counselor. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Vermont Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Vermont Legal Aid, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Project; Department of Disabilities, Aging and Independent Living, Adult Protective Services
description: Advocacy for people in licensed long-term care facilities and people getting care at home through Choices for Care. Adult Protective Services takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults.
next_step: Call the ombudsman at 1-800-889-2047, extension 3, or use the online form. To report abuse, call your local or state police and Adult Protective Services at 1-800-564-1612. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for older Vermonters
organization: Vermont Legal Aid, Elder Law Project; Legal Services Vermont
description: Vermont Legal Aid’s Elder Law Project gives free civil legal help to Vermonters 60 and older: abuse and financial exploitation, housing and benefits, and individual rights and advance planning. Legal Services Vermont runs the statewide helpline.
next_step: Call the statewide legal helpline at 1-800-889-2047, or ask for help online at vtlawhelp.org.
constraints: Offices have limited in-person hours; call or use the online form first.

name: VA health care in Vermont
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA White River Junction Healthcare System
description: Vermont veterans are served by the VA White River Junction Healthcare System: the White River Junction VA Medical Center (163 Veterans Drive, White River Junction; 802-295-9363, toll-free 866-687-8387) and its outpatient clinics.
next_step: Call 802-295-9363 or 866-687-8387 for appointments or the 24-hour nurse line. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.

name: Vermont Center for Independent Living
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Main office: 11 East State Street, Montpelier, VT 05602. Toll-free 800-639-1522; Relay 711.
Other offices: Burlington 802-861-2896; Morrisville 802-888-2180; Bennington 802-447-0574; Brattleboro 802-254-6851; Newport 802-334-9000 (call for an appointment); Rutland 802-779-9021.

name: Veterans Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-ZZ-041): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 508-791-1213.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.
